note: Both sets read the same five spanwise curves and share the same flaws: duplicated prebend/twist entries, conflicting chord values at the tip (1.5 m and 0.6 m both stated at r/R = 1.0), and quotes that are only axis labels or panel captions. Set A adds a gross error — relative thickness 20 % at r/R = 0.0, where the curve is at 100 % (20 is the axis floor) — whereas Set B instead adds a correct chord reading (~5.7 m at r/R = 0.25) and only a redundant 20 % thickness entry at the tip. Set B is therefore the more faithful set, although both misplace the chord value 5.2 m (the root value) onto r/R = 0.2 and both give 14 deg and 15 deg twist at the root.
remarks: The text layer contains only axis labels and captions, so every numeric claim is a visual curve reading with inherent tolerance (I used roughly ±0.5 m chord, ±1.5 deg twist, ±3 % thickness). Shared problems in both sets: chord 5.2 m bound to r/R = 0.2 (that is the r/R = 0 value; the peak near r/R = 0.2 is ~5.8 m, which neither set captures), chord 1.5 m and 0.6 m both at r/R = 1.0 (the curve drops to ~0.5 m at the very tip), twist 14 deg and 15 deg both at r/R = 0.0, prebend 0 m at 0.0 and -4 m at 1.0 each stated twice, twist -2 deg at 0.85 stated twice, and several quotes that contain no supporting numbers (e.g. '(c) Twist', '(b) Relative thickness'). B's 'relative thickness 20 % at r/R = 1.0' duplicates its own 22 % entry at the same station; counted as a duplicate rather than a misread since the curve is ~22 %.
